relevance.rationale: Join CORRECT: the file is the NIST complete listing for the 2022 adjustment, matching the registered dataset entry. Not present in the working tree on this branch — recovered from the intake commit blob (git show 6131f6d019:uploads/codata-2022-constants.txt); sha matches the intake record. The key is heavily and genuinely load-bearing: it is the sole source cited for every reference mass in folio/quantum-observable-universe/mass-theory/mass-from-generators.lean:35-59,204 and for local-substrate-q.lean:94, knot-particle-generation.lean:128, plus 5 .ts cites arrays. BUT the citation is NOT load-bearing at the numbers it labels: six of the seven mass literals in mass-from-generators.lean are CODATA-2018, not 2022. From this document: m_e = 0.51099895069 (Lean has 0.51099895000, -1.35 ppb); m_p = 938.27208943 (Lean 938.27208816, -1.35 ppb); m_n = 939.56542194 (Lean 939.56542052, -1.51 ppb); deuteron 1875.61294500 (Lean 1875.61294257); helion 2808.39161112 (Lean 2808.39160743); alpha 3727.3794118 (Lean 3727.37940824). Only the muon (105.6583755) matches. The same stale values sit in computations/substrate/experimental_constants.py:55,58 under a header that explicitly claims 'CODATA 2022', and its n-p difference 1.2933321 +/- 0.0000005 is the 2018 value where this document gives 1.29333251 +/- 0.00000038 (a 317 ppb shift on Delta_np, itself one of the L2-failing observables). Corpus-grep run: docs/audits/2026-06-30-codata-literals-rollup-precision-partition.md treats 938.27208816 as an 'exact-value match' to the registry and does NOT record that it is the 2018 value; no audit, content block, computations file, or docs/coordination ledger records this 2018-vs-2022 discrepancy for m_p/m_n/deuteron/helion/alpha. Scope-(a): this document, as read, does not support the seven literals it is cited for; that is a data-currency finding, not a claim that any downstream derivation is wrong.
